items.title: A Pipeline-Parallel System for Depth-Recurrent Models
items.summary: O artigo compartilhado pela Hugging Face aborda o sistema de paralelismo de pipeline (pipeline parallelism) necessário para o escalonamento de modelos de recorrência de profundidade (depth-recurrent). Nesses modelos, onde pilhas de blocos compartilhados são usadas várias vezes, propõe-se uma solução para as limitações que o método tradicional 1F1B enfrenta no gerenciamento do fluxo de dados cíclico.

snapshot.description: Depth-recurrent (Looped) models raise effective depth by applying a shared stack of blocks several times. Scaling them usually requires pipeline parallelism, but commonly used interleaved 1F1B is drawn for an acyclic stage graph in which each micro-batch enters each stage once. We introduce SWEEP-Bench, a simulation benchmark with 80 conveyor-belt manipulation tasks spanning 16 skill categories, each evaluated at 13 belt speeds (0.10-0.40 m/s). snapshot.description: How much interaction experience is needed to distill a capable visual agent? We study learning from few tasks and recorded interaction histories. Our framework selects representative trajectories using skill-context coverage and ordered visual-decision similarity. On-policy distillation (OPD) learns through fresh interaction on selected tasks or fresh student responses at fixed histories. items.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Embodied-Harness apresenta uma estrutura de agente duplo que melhora o processo de execução em tarefas de manipulação robótica sem atualizar os parâmetros do modelo. O objetivo é superar as limitações de gerenciamento de memória e repetição de experiência de agentes baseados em modelos de visão-linguagem (vision-language model) com um mecanismo de reflexão (reflector) que analisa as evidências de execução.

snapshot.description: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters.
